title: Optimal Convergence Rates for the Spectrum of the Graph Laplacian on Poisson Point Clouds
reviewed_version: arXiv:2312.08149v1, submitted2023-12-13; PDF author date2023-12-14;23pages. Journal-version equivalence not asserted.
inspection_outcome: Four Major analytical/probability/proof issues and one Minor negative-norm definition correction in the acquired preprint.
summary: The uniform relative-L2 point-sampling input estimate admits a smooth localized counterexample. Variational concentration fails on the stated full continuous trial class and iid sampling is unavailable after cluster selection. Individual eigenvector control lacks multiplicity/projection treatment. Pointwise proof drops random multipliers and the first-order corrector. Correct reciprocal scaling and conditional positive components are retained; final journal and properly corrected Poisson spectral theorem are not declared false.
limitations: All scientific conclusions apply only to acquired arXivv1 bytes; no final journal equivalence or independent acceptance.
External AV23b,Flu95,AKM19 and other imported results were not independently retrieved or fully certified; faults in this restatement/use do not refute those works.
P1 refutes the literal uniform point-sampling input, and P2 refutes a required uniform trial-class comparison. Neither establishes that the intended corrected spectral rate is impossible.
The finite matrix is a perturbation-logic diagnostic, not a constructed Poisson realization.
P3/P4 replacement projection, uniform stochastic, boundary and corrector estimates remain unproved; no complete repair certified.
No author code or simulation executed; symbolic local quadratic and exact rational matrix checks are reviewer-authored support.
Historical conversation-only output remains unavailable, not declared absent.
repair_verification: Counterexamples checked with full hypotheses and source quantifiers. Correct residual identity, negative pairing, inverse-eigenvalue algebra and wavelength scaling verified. Complete corrected probabilistic/spectral/pointwise theorem not certified.

issues.claim: Uniform relative-L2 bound for every smooth sampled Dirichlet input is false.
issues.decisive_evidence: Smooth quadratic cutoff at an isolated interior sample gives zero sampled values, forcing e_x0, fixed nonzero graph solution, while continuum norm tends0 asrho^(2+d/2).
issues.counterevidence: Uses intended boundary convention and smooth functions; no reliance on Sobolev representative ambiguity; external cited theorem not assessed.
issues.correction: State correct sampling/coarse-graining, data regularity and estimate, then recheck variational uses.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: Theorem 1.1 has one pathwise scale/event for every H2 Dirichlet input. A smooth quadratic cutoff around one isolated interior sample has zero sampled values but fixed nonzero sampled elliptic forcing, hence a fixed nonzero discrete Dirichlet solution. Its continuum L2 norm tends to zero as the cutoff shrinks, contradicting the displayed relative-L2 estimate. Smoothness avoids Sobolev representative objections; the construction is graph-adapted only under the actual uniform quantifier.

issues.claim: Cluster iid premise and fixed-to-uniform variational concentration do not justify spectral comparison.
issues.decisive_evidence: Selected connected component is dependent; constant-based smooth cutoffs in d>=3 retain continuum norm1, supcap and arbitrarily small energy while empirical norm is0 or arbitrarily small.
issues.counterevidence: A valid fixed-function theorem is not refuted; deterministic finite test-space or operator methods may repair. T-dependent event and deferred induction are not supplied.
issues.correction: Actual-cluster concentration, controlled approximation space/maps, simultaneous events and noncircular T/induction closure.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The largest well-connected selected cluster is not an iid uniform sample; the displayed Bernstein expression also omits a bounded-range term/hypotheses. More decisively, in d>=3 smooth cutoffs of a normalized constant can vanish at every finite graph point while retaining continuum norm, bounded sup norm and arbitrarily small energy. Choosing a permitted domain/cap with slack meets (2.8), and small positive sampled values avoid zero denominators. Thus fixed-function estimates cannot control the broad variational maxima. Maximizing over T loses the T-dependent event, and the unproved orthogonality transfer plus extra scale factor in (2.36) remain central gaps. Final optimal spectral rates are not claimed mathematically disproved by these gaps.

issues.claim: Single-vector bound and residual test do not handle repeated eigenvalues or the resonant operator.
issues.decisive_evidence: Allowed multiple continuum spectra; exact diag(lambda,lambda,nu) perturbation rotates split vectors byfixed angle despite vanishing operator error. Correct residual has L+lambda and negative corrector term.
issues.counterevidence: Matrix is not asserted to be a Poisson model; principal eigenvalue simple, eigenvalue and cluster convergence may remain valid.
issues.correction: Simple-eigenvalue hypothesis with isolation/orientation, or whole-cluster projection/alignment theorem; correct residual and track gap.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The actual gap excludes equal eigenvalues and permitted domains can have multiplicities. It cannot select or uniquely approximate an arbitrary prescribed vector inside a repeated eigenspace; a rotating split 3x3 matrix is used only as an abstract spectral diagnostic, not as a Poisson-graph realization. Independently, substitution of L phi_m=-lambda_m phi_m into the stated two-scale error yields L+lambda_m and a negative corrector term, contrary to (2.25). The resonant equation needs a projected/coercive argument. These damage the central eigenvector derivation.

issues.claim: Local stochastic estimates do not establish deterministic all-vertex/every-edge bound as written.
issues.decisive_evidence: X(x)^(d/2) edge and X(x)^2 pointwise multipliers are dropped; local radius hypothesis not uniform; phi_m=w+phi0+corrector but final triangle omits corrector.
issues.counterevidence: Tail integrability does not imply deterministic eventual coefficient; no actual Poisson eigenfunction counterexample claimed. Corrected stochastic/interior theorem may be possible.
issues.correction: Retain/control random factors, spatial events, corrector, boundary region, wavelength and gap dependence.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The source applies local regularity only above a center-dependent random minimal scale, then drops X(x)^(d/2) and X(x)^2 factors when asserting deterministic all-vertex/every-edge estimates. Its final triangle inequality also omits the explicit corrector from phi_m=w+phi_0+corrector. The displayed wavelength rescaling is inconsistent with the eigenvalue equation, and convex domains allow corners so unrestricted near-boundary Hessian control is unavailable. These are central derivation failures; no replacement theorem or general nonexistence result is claimed.

issues.claim: Printed negative-norm formula uses H1 pairing and equals H1 on Dirichlet functions.
issues.decisive_evidence: Cauchy-Schwarz plusg=f gives exact equality toH1norm.
issues.counterevidence: Later proof uses intended L2 duality, indicating local definition repair; correcting it does not settle central findings.
issues.correction: Use distributional/L2 numerator with consistent normalized convention.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The displayed H^-1 definition pairs f with g in the H1 inner product. On Dirichlet functions Cauchy-Schwarz and g=f give exactly the H1 norm, not the intended negative norm. Later estimates use the L2 duality pairing, which determines the local correction.

findings.title: The scalar eigenvector conclusion lacks a multiplicity and resonance argument
locations: p.14, residual identity (2.25) and the proposed testing step
pp.17-18, Step 3 and uniqueness assertion after (2.35)
findings.claim_checked: Theorem 1.2 bounds one discrete eigenvector against one continuum eigenfunction, with a denominator equal to the distance to the nearest distinct eigenvalue. The theorem covers all admissible k and does not require the continuum eigenvalue to be simple. Step 3 treats the higher-index eigenvector proof as the principal case with notation changes.
analytic_check: Allowed convex/C^{1,1} domains do not ensure simple continuum spectrum. For a positive definite constant coefficient matrix A, a linear image A^{1/2}B of a ball transforms -div(A grad) to the ordinary Dirichlet Laplacian on the ball, which has higher eigenspaces of dimension greater than one in d>=2. Thus multiplicity is a genuine allowed case, not merely a possible graph degeneracy.

If E_lambda has dimension r>1, removing the component along one chosen phi_0,k leaves r-1 resonant directions in E_lambda. The gap to the nearest distinct eigenvalue controls the orthogonal complement of the entire E_lambda, not the complement of one vector. The scalar pairing normalization in (1.10) does not remove those remaining directions.

Exact perturbation diagnostic: A_0=diag(2,2,5), A_epsilon=[[2,epsilon,0],[epsilon,2,0],[0,0,5]]. The gap from the repeated eigenvalue 2 to the distinct eigenvalue is 3 and ||A_epsilon-A_0||=epsilon. The two split eigenvectors normalized to have inner product 1 with e_1 are e_1-e_2 and e_1+e_2. Each remains at distance 1 from e_1 for every epsilon>0. The eigenvalues nevertheless converge with error epsilon.

The diagnostic is a counterexample to the scalar perturbation inference under only a distinct-cluster gap. It is not asserted to be an actual Poisson-point-cloud counterexample. A graph-specific result would require a further selection or alignment theorem that is not supplied in this version.

Actual p.18 states that the maximizer in (2.35) is unique. At the start of a multiple eigenvalue block, every unit vector in the remaining eigenspace is a maximizer. Even after ignoring the harmless sign ambiguity, the asserted uniqueness fails in the allowed multiple-eigenvalue case.

Actual p.14 prints (L-lambda_m)w and a +lambda_m*c corrector term, where w=phi_m-(phi_0+c), L phi_m=-lambda_m phi_m, and div(A grad phi_0)=-lambda_bar phi_0. Direct expansion instead gives (L+lambda_m)w=-L(phi_0+c)+div(A grad phi_0)+(lambda_bar-lambda_m)phi_0-lambda_m*c. Both signs must be corrected.

The corrected operator L+lambda_m is resonant at the target eigenvalue. Testing the equation with an unrestricted w does not itself yield the claimed spectral-gap coercivity. A projection argument is required even in the simple-eigenvalue case; for multiplicity it must project off the whole eigenspace.
counterevidence_considered: The principal Dirichlet eigenvalue on a connected domain is simple, so this multiplicity objection does not apply to the base eigenvalue itself.

Ordered eigenvalue estimates and Courant-Fischer principles can remain meaningful with multiplicities. This finding targets the scalar eigenvector statement and its proof, not the possibility of an eigenvalue convergence theorem.

One could instead choose a continuum vector depending on the projected discrete eigenspace, or formulate convergence of spectral projectors. That changes or completes the statement and requires a cluster argument; it is not established by the printed scalar normalization.
No false normalization defect is inferred merely from extracted sum glyphs: the source explicitly defines normalized empirical sums on p.8.
findings.impact: The stated scalar eigenvector conclusion is not justified for the full theorem scope, and the displayed residual proof is not algebraically valid as printed.
findings.repair: State and prove the simple-eigenvalue case with the necessary spectral isolation and nonzero pairing, or formulate a whole-cluster eigenspace/projector estimate with a rigorous alignment convention. Correct both signs in (2.25), project away from the resonant eigenspace, and track gap-dependent constants and admissible scale conditions.
findings.scope_limit: No probabilistic graph counterexample to the intended convergence rate is claimed. This is a demonstrated missing hypothesis/argument plus a directly checked algebraic error.

findings.title: The variational proof requires an impossible uniform empirical norm estimate on its stated competitor class
locations: p.10, full continuous competitor class and (2.8)
pp.17-19, deferred comparison and induction closure
findings.attribution: Root independently proposed the finite-sample cutoff witness; this native auxiliary read the actual competitor quantifiers, inspected the printed pages, and analytically corroborated it. The other native auxiliary separately checks Appendix A's independence assumptions; that external-to-this-scope conclusion is not adopted without its own receipt.
findings.claim_checked: The proof applies a concentration bound for the empirical norm while retaining a maximum over all continuous competitors satisfying the broad L2, L-infinity and gradient conditions in (2.8). It subsequently applies related estimates to the even broader A_T class.
analytic_check: Fix d>=3 and a realization with finitely many sample points in U_m. Let phi be a smooth normalized continuum ground-state representative lying within the intended factor-four bounds of (2.8). Around each sample point choose disjoint balls with radii tending to zero, and smooth cutoffs that vanish at the point and equal one outside its ball.

The cost of each cutoff in squared H^1 seminorm is O(rho^{d-2}), and its L2 cost tends to zero. Because the sample is finite, the product cutoff times phi converges to phi in H^1 and L2 while vanishing at every sampled point. Normalize its continuum averaged L2 norm to one. For sufficiently small radii the L-infinity bound and the factor-four gradient slack are retained.

The resulting continuous competitor has continuum normalized L2 norm one and empirical squared norm zero. For nonzero Rayleigh denominators, replace exact zeros by arbitrarily small values at all sample points; the empirical squared norm remains arbitrarily small while the same continuum bounds hold.

Thus no realization can satisfy the uniform estimate |empirical_mean(f^2)-1|<=epsilon<1 over the stated full competitor class. The fact that the constructed f depends on the realized cloud is exactly why a pointwise-in-f concentration estimate cannot be moved through that maximum.

Actual p.11 keeps the maximum in (2.12) and (2.13) and explicitly applies the concentration expression to general f. Actual Lemma A.2 on p.19 is only a statement for phi_0,k. The source does not restrict the maximum to finitely many fixed spectral functions or provide a uniform empirical-process argument.

The A_T class on p.12 imposes only continuity, normalized L2 and a fixed L-infinity bound. It still permits the same interpolation at finite sample points and therefore does not repair the uniformity problem.
counterevidence_considered: A forward lower bound can sometimes be proved by testing only the single deterministic continuum ground state. That possible alternative does not validate the maximum-based estimates or the reverse bound as printed.

Even if one replaced the connectivity-selected cloud by independent points, the failure of a uniform law over this unrestricted class would remain. It is logically distinct from the Appendix's proposed iid model.

The cutoff witness requires d>=3 for the elementary O(rho^{d-2}) construction, and that is already within the theorem's asserted scope. No two-dimensional cutoff extension is needed for this conclusion.

If the literal gradient threshold in (2.8) itself excludes the ground state because an ellipticity factor is omitted, the preceding variational restriction already fails. The cutoff argument applies under the charitable intended interpretation in which the ground state has the advertised strict factor-four slack.

supporting_closure_gaps.check: The displayed failure probability contains T^2 in its denominator. Independence of the numerical upper bound from T is not independence of the event from T. Maximizing over all T therefore does not preserve the displayed probability.

supporting_closure_gaps.location: p.17, choice of T after the pointwise bound
supporting_closure_gaps.check: The displayed pointwise estimate explicitly uses (2.24), whose proof uses eigenvalue estimate (2.23), while p.13 says (2.23) is conditional on a suitable m-independent T choice. The text supplies no independent bootstrap or stopping argument to close this dependency.

The comparison between discrete and continuum orthogonality is granted 'for the moment'. The proof ends after (2.40) without proving the deferred claim, controlling its normalization, or explaining gap factors in the resulting Rayleigh estimate. This is a missing proof step, not here asserted to be an impossible comparison after suitable reformulation.

The printed normalized L2 competitor additionally has L-infinity norm at most 4*C_0*3^{-2m}*lambda_0,K^{d/4}. For fixed K and sufficiently large m the upper bound is below 1, whereas normalized averaged L2 norm one implies L-infinity norm at least 1. The printed class is empty. Removing the extraneous 3^{-2m} is a local repair, but does not cure the uniform probability gap.

findings.impact: The acquired preprint's variational proof does not establish the asserted uniform high-probability eigenvalue bounds. The cutoff witness directly refutes the required uniform empirical normalization step, not the intended spectral convergence rate itself.
findings.repair: Use fixed deterministic spectral test spaces or another class with justified uniform sampling control; provide an appropriate concentration result for the actual selected cluster; prove the reverse variational bound and deferred orthogonality comparison; and close the T and eigenvector dependencies without circularity. Correct the scaling in (2.36).
findings.scope_limit: This supports the parent's combined empirical/variational probability finding. It is not an additional claim that the intended eigenvalue theorem is necessarily false.

additional_repair_notes.title: The printed H^{-1} definition uses the energy inner product
additional_repair_notes.check: For a nonzero zero-boundary f, sup_g |<f,g>_{H^1}|/||g||_{H^1}=||f||_{H^1}. Thus the displayed definition is the H^1 norm, not the dual norm of the L2 functional g -> <f,g>_{L2}. Formula (2.38) uses the latter duality. For a low Dirichlet eigenmode, the generic L2 duality bound with the printed norm fails by an inverse eigenvalue factor, up to a fixed edge-counting constant.
additional_repair_notes.repair: Define H^{-1} through the normalized L2 pairing. This is a local correction supporting the proof audit, not an independent Major finding.
additional_repair_notes.limitation: The low-mode calculation diagnoses the underlying duality inequality; it is not presented as a direct counterexample to every constrained pair f,g in (2.38).

additional_repair_notes.title: The inverse Rayleigh quotient is confused with the Dirichlet energy
additional_repair_notes.check: From (2.5), the inverse-operator quotient at the normalized eigenfunction is mu_0,1=3^{2m}/lambda_0,1. The displayed identity instead equates it with the gradient energy and 3^{-2m}lambda_0,1. The later argument often uses the correct reciprocal variable, so this is recorded as a formula repair rather than a separate theorem refutation.
additional_repair_notes.repair: Separate the energy identity, including the coefficient matrix, from the inverse Rayleigh quotient.

positive_checks.check: Under the intended interior/boundary Dirichlet convention, -L is a symmetric positive finite-dimensional operator on interior values, its inverse has positive reciprocal eigenvalues, and the continuum inverse is compact and self-adjoint. Courant-Fischer comparison is a suitable general framework. Local boundary and index typography is not interpreted as a new spectral phenomenon.

Conditional on |mu_m-mu_0|<=C*q_m*sqrt(mu_0) with q_m=1 for d>=3 and sqrt(m) for d=2, the conversion to relative eigenvalue error is correct once C*q_m/sqrt(mu_0)<=1/2. Indeed |3^{2m}lambda_m-lambda_0|/lambda_0=|mu_m-mu_0|/mu_m<=2C*q_m*3^{-m}sqrt(lambda_0). This has the scaling claimed in (1.9). The preceding probabilistic premise remains unproved in the present text.

The paper explicitly declares normalized empirical sums and averaged L2 conventions. No defect is inferred from extraction of a barred-sum glyph as an ordinary sum. Nonzero scalar pairing suffices to rescale a single simple eigenvector, but it does not align a multiple eigenspace.
Multiplicity itself does not invalidate ordered eigenvalues or cluster convergence. The substantive distinction is between eigenvalue/eigenspace control and control of a specified individual vector.

checks.topic: Random graph, normalization and event quantifiers
details: The intended graph joins Poisson points at distance at most one, with intensity alpha>alpha_c(d) and d>=2. The selected eta_*(U) is a largest connected component defined through a well-connected enclosing cube; it is not the entire homogeneous Poisson sample in U.
The intended domain assumption is convex or C^(1,1), with U_m=3^m U0. The estimates use normalized/averaged continuum and discrete norms; bar-sum notation is defined explicitly on PDF8.

Theorem1.3 claims a deterministic C(d,alpha) for every admissible m,k and every indicated vertex/edge, using the random threshold from Theorem1.2. A per-center random estimate with stretched-exponential tails has weaker quantifiers.
The denominator dist(zeta,U0) in(1.13) is zero for zeta in U0 and is an evident missing-boundary-symbol typo; the substantive review interprets the intended dist(zeta,partial U0).

checks.topic: Lemma A.1 eigenfunction bound and coefficient dependence
details: The familiar Moser/heat-semigroup argument yields an L2-to-Linfinity eigenfunction bound with eigenvalue exponent d/4 for a fixed uniformly elliptic constant coefficient operator. The normalization on a domain contained in the unit cube is compatible with the bound: unnormalized L2 is |U0|^(1/2) times the averaged norm.

The ellipticity dependence should be retained. Under A=tI, the eigenfunction is unchanged and lambda=t*lambda_Laplace, so a universal constant independent of t cannot bound the eigenfunction by C(d)*lambda^(d/4) with no coefficient factor. At fixed alpha one can allow C(d,alpha), as the main theorems do.
The supplied proof is a citation to [Flu95, Proposition5], not a self-contained derivation. No claim is made to have checked that external paper or all its hypotheses.
The scaling psi(y)=phi(3^m y) preserves averaged L2 normalization and changes the eigenvalue from3^(-2m)lambda0 to lambda0.

checks.assessment_note: Appendix concentration derivation and its uniform use are not justified; see L0447-F1.
details: PDF20 asserts that values at points of3^(-m)eta_*(U_m) are independent identically distributed variables with uniform-domain variance. That does not follow from the underlying Poisson law after connectivity selection.

For a selected component containing exactly two vertices, their distance must be at most one. Two independent uniform points in a domain of diameter greater than one have positive probability of larger separation. More generally connected selected configurations have geometric constraints absent from an iid conditional Poisson sample. Thus replacing the selected component by iid uniform samples is invalid.

Even for genuinely independent bounded centered variables, the general Bernstein bound contains a boundedness term Mt/3 in addition to the variance; a pure variance denominator for every t>0 requires an additional hypothesis not supplied here. For example, a Bernoulli variable of mean p=1/100, N=1, and t=99/100 has upper-tail probability1/100 while2 exp(-t^2/(2p(1-p)))=2 exp(-49.5)<1/100. This illustrates failure of the invoked generic inequality, not a counterexample to the particular eigenfunction statement.

The cardinality on the right side of(A.3) is random while the probability is unconditional; conditioning or a separate count event is also needed for the displayed expression to define the intended deterministic bound.

Lemma A.3 explicitly reuses the same argument, so it inherits the sampling-law problem. This does not by itself disprove a properly formulated fixed-eigenfunction concentration estimate for the actual cluster.

checks.assessment_note: Decisive uniform-obstruction argument supplied by parent and verified analytically here; constant-function version strengthens the boundary-condition bookkeeping.
checks.topic: Concentration cannot pass through the variational maximum
details: The use at(2.12)-(2.13) and(2.19)-(2.22) requires one event controlling empirical quadrature for every competitor in the maximum. A fixed deterministic-function tail bound is insufficient. The class A_T in(2.20) contains all continuous averaged-L2-normalized functions subject only to a supremum cap; it is not a finite-dimensional fixed space.

For any finite realized sample set {x_i} in an open bounded domain and d>=3, choose disjoint small balls about its points and smooth cutoffs chi_i that vanish at x_i and equal1 outside each ball. Let h_r be the product of these cutoffs. Then h_r->1 in averaged L2, 0<=h_r<=1, and the averaged Dirichlet energy tends to0 because each cutoff contributes O(r_i^(d-2)) and the number of points is finite.

Normalize f_r=h_r/||h_r||_(averaged L2). Then f_r has continuum norm1, supnorm tending to1, arbitrarily small positive gradient energy, and f_r(x_i)=0 for every sample. Thus whenever the stated supremum cap has strict slack above1, f_r satisfies that cap and any positive energy cap in(2.8), while its empirical squared norm is0 rather than close to1. Such a strict cap is certainly available in A_T for sufficiently large T; an allowed sufficiently small domain makes the displayed lambda-dependent cap strict as well.

Replace h_r by h_r+tau for tau>0 and renormalize if an empirical denominator must be nonzero. The discrete norm is then positive and arbitrarily small, while the continuum norm and all strict bounds persist. Therefore excluding zero denominators does not repair the uniform comparison.

The competitor is chosen after the finite sample is realized, exactly as allowed by a pathwise maximum. This is a deterministic obstruction to the claimed simultaneous comparison; it does not contradict a concentration theorem stated only for one fixed, sample-independent function.

The same argument works even for an unselected independent point cloud. It is logically distinct from the connectivity-dependence gap but belongs to the same failed quadrature step in the final synthesis.

checks.assessment_note: Correct scaling and regularity scope identified; the printed Hessian argument is not certified.
details: Write L=3^m and lambda_bar=L^(-2)lambda0. If -div A grad phi=lambda_bar phi, the correct unit-frequency coordinate is y=x+(L/sqrt(lambda0))z. Under the printed map y=x+sqrt(lambda0)z, the transformed equation instead has eigenvalue L^(-2)lambda0^2, not1.

Interior derivative bounds require an interior ball at the chosen wavelength or an explicit distance-to-boundary loss. They do not automatically justify the sum of suprema over every B1(x) in(2.26), including points whose balls meet the boundary.

The allowed convex class need not have bounded Hessians. In a circular sector of opening omega in(pi/2,pi), the positive Dirichlet mode u(r,theta)=J_nu(j_(nu,1)r)sin(nu theta), nu=pi/omega in(1,2), behaves as c*r^nu sin(nu theta) near the corner. Its Hessian behaves as r^(nu-2) and is unbounded. A linear change by A^(1/2) gives the same convex-domain example for any fixed SPD coefficient matrix.

This is a counterexample to a blanket boundary Hessian-sup justification, not to the theorem's interior pointwise estimate. A valid derivation would retain distance restrictions, use a suitable boundary cutoff, or use the appropriate integrable derivative estimates from the imported homogenization theorem.

Imported corrector and large-scale regularity results [AV23b] were not independently read here. Their exact hypotheses, gauges and probability quantifiers cannot be inferred from a citation or relabeled as newly verified.

checks.assessment_note: The deterministic all-vertex/all-edge conclusion does not follow from the displayed local random estimates; see L0447-F2.
checks.topic: Theorem1.3 random factors, domain of applicability and corrector term
details: Equation(2.27) applies only with R=(L/2)dist(y,partial U0) at least the local random scale X and r in[X,R/2]; using r=X requires R>=2X. Theorem1.3 itself has no corresponding interior-scale restriction.

The final edge estimate on PDF16 retains the multiplier X^(d/2). The text concludes the deterministic bound from X^(d/2)=O_s(C). Stretched-exponential integrability is not an almost-sure deterministic bound. PDF17 likewise retains X(zeta)^4 in the squared pointwise remainder estimate and then omits it in the conclusion.

Logical counterexample to that inference: take an unbounded exponential random variable X, which has X=O_1(2), and define a_m=X^(d/2)*3^(-m). No deterministic K and almost-sure finite threshold Y(X) can make a_m<=K*3^(-m) for every3^m>Y(X), because on the positive-probability event X^(d/2)>K the inequality fails for every m. This is a counterexample to the absorption step, not a constructed Poisson eigenfunction counterexample.

A per-center stretched-exponential bound also does not provide a uniform bound on the collection X(x) over all vertices of growing domains. A separate spatial probability argument, retained random multiplier, or stronger estimate is required.

The remainder is defined as w=phi_m-(phi0+sum_i partial_i phi0*corrector_i). Hence phi_m=w+phi0+sum_i partial_i phi0*corrector_i. The displayed triangle inequality on PDF17 drops the last term. Bounding w alone does not prove(1.12), and it does not establish the deterministic supremum bound used to fix T in(2.20).

A corrected local stochastic estimate may still be possible if the corrector term, random multipliers, boundary regime and spectral projection are handled. None of those omitted steps is assumed completed in this receipt.

checks.assessment_note: Formal identities checked; dependent quantitative estimates remain subject to findings above and core-helper spectral checks.
checks.topic: Positive conditional components of the later proof
details: The discrete product identity (fg)(x)-(fg)(y)=((f(x)+f(y))/2)(g(x)-g(y))+((g(x)+g(y))/2)(f(x)-f(y)) is exact.

With the intended standard H^(-1) norm based on L2 duality and a valid ball Poincare inequality, ||phi||_(H^-1(B_t))<=C*t*||phi||infinity. Combining an eigenvalue error O(L^-3 lambda0^(3/2)) with an eigenfunction bound O(lambda0^(d/4)) gives the displayed scaling O(L^-3 lambda0^(d/4+3/2)t) in term B, conditional on those inputs.
The change of variables F(y)=f(Ly), v0(y)=L^-2 u0(Ly) in(A.6) is correct for averaged continuum norms and empirical means. It transforms the quadrature difference by the factor L^2.

For an unselected homogeneous Poisson process conditional on its count, the point locations would be iid uniform. That fact explains the intended Monte Carlo heuristic, but does not supply it for the selected connected component.
No new numerical or symbolic execution was necessary for these exact analytic checks.

checks.assessment_note: Duplicated central issues are assigned to the parent/core rather than independently counted here.
details: The L2 eigenvector estimate explicitly contains the reciprocal gap to the nearest distinct eigenvalue. Theorem1.3 omits that factor, and the extension from the ground state to all k requires attention to multiplicities and eigenbasis alignment. Core helper is responsible for that central issue; no arbitrary-eigenvector convergence is certified here.

From L phi_m=-lambda_m phi_m and w=phi_m-v one gets (L+lambda_m)w=-L v-lambda_m v. Thus the printed(L-lambda_m) identity and positive last corrector term in(2.25) do not match the definitions. With the correct sign the eigenvalue operator is resonant and needs an orthogonality/projection argument. This was communicated to the core helper and is not a third later finding.

PDF8 defines H^-1 with an H1 numerator, whereas PDF16 uses the intended L2 pairing. Treating the printed numerator literally would not give the standard negative norm. This is recorded as a notation correction, not used to manufacture a separate theorem counterexample.

In dimension2, (A.5) includes an extra L^-2 factor on the quadrature error that is absent in its application(2.16). As written it does not deliver that application. This scaling discrepancy is retained as an editorial/derivation qualification within the quadrature issue.

checks.topic: Later extensions, optimality and computational scope
details: The discussion of second-order rates cites numerical work by others and says that the explanation is not pursued in this paper. It does not report newly performed experiments.

Extensions to general manifolds and the Neumann spectrum are described in prose. The appendix and supplied proof address the specified Dirichlet Euclidean setting; this helper does not certify those extensions or the treatment of a Neumann zero mode.

Matching an upper bound's powers with earlier homogenization results is not itself a lower-bound proof for every eigenfunction/domain. No new optimality counterexample is claimed; the exact scope of the word optimal is kept distinct from the verified formulas.

The source manifest says optional code and supplements were not located in a bounded historical search. This is not an exhaustive absence assertion, and no missing-code mathematical defect is inferred.

findings.assessment_note: Central concentration/quadrature proof failure; fixed-function cluster estimates and final corrected spectral theorem are not claimed refuted.
findings.title: The appendix uses an iid law unavailable for the selected cluster, and the spectral proof requires a false uniform quadrature comparison
locations: Use through the maxima at(2.12)-(2.13) and(2.19)-(2.22), PDF11-13
decisive_evidence: The selected eta_*(U) is a largest connected component, not the full Poisson process. Conditional on selecting two vertices, connectedness forces their mutual distance<=1, contradicting the unqualified iid-uniform model used in the variance and Bernstein calculation.

Even granting a valid fixed-function concentration result, finite-sample cutoff functions can have continuum normalized L2 norm1, arbitrarily small energy and bounded supremum, yet vanish at every sampled point. A tiny positive perturbation makes the empirical denominator positive but arbitrarily small. Hence no realization can support the simultaneous norm comparison for the whole displayed variational class where the cap has strict slack.
findings.analytic_proof: For d>=3, start with constant1 and multiply smooth cutoffs vanishing in disjoint radius-r_i neighborhoods of the finitely many samples. The squared L2 difference tends to0 with total removed volume, while gradient energy is O(sum r_i^(d-2)). Normalize in averaged L2. Supnorm tends to1, energy tends to0, and empirical norm is0. The competitor space requires C intersect L2, not a zero trace. A_T for large T supplies strict supnorm slack; any positive energy constraint can simultaneously be satisfied. Add a small constant before normalization to avoid a zero denominator.
findings.attribution: Parent first identified the finite-sample cutoff obstruction; native helper independently checked the analytic mechanism and provided the constant-function/no-zero-trace variant. This is collaborative initial review, not independent acceptance.
counterevidence_and_limits: For an actual unselected Poisson sample conditional on count, iid sampling is available; that is a different sampling law from eta_*(U).

A concentration theorem for one fixed eigenfunction may still be true for the selected cluster by a suitable dependent-point-process argument. The cutoff example is sample-dependent and addresses the maximum, not such a fixed-function theorem.
Corrected spectral convergence could be proved by another approximation/operator framework. No final journal theorem or the external [AV23b] paper is assessed here.
findings.impact: The probabilistic estimates invoked to compare the continuum/discrete variational maxima do not justify that core step. This affects the asserted spectral rates on which the later pointwise estimates depend.
findings.recommended_action: Use a justified concentration or homogenization estimate for the actual selected process and an approximation space/operator comparison that does not demand impossible uniform quadrature over all continuous bounded competitors. State all simultaneous event quantifiers.

findings.assessment_note: Unsupported derivation of the stated deterministic sup/edge bounds; no constructed counterexample to a properly corrected theorem.
findings.title: Theorem1.3's proof loses local random multipliers and the first-order corrector when passing to deterministic bounds
locations: Pointwise remainder estimate and triangle inequality, PDF17
decisive_evidence: The edge proof yields a bound with X^(d/2), and the squared pointwise proof yields a bound with X(zeta)^4. The stated conclusion instead uses deterministic C(d,alpha), justified only by stretched-exponential integrability. Integrability does not remove these multipliers or make them uniform over all growing-domain vertices.

For an unbounded X=O_1(2), a_m=X^(d/2)3^(-m) cannot satisfy a_m<=K3^(-m) eventually for deterministic K on the positive-probability event X^(d/2)>K. This rigorously isolates the invalid logical absorption step.

The proof defines w=phi_m-phi0-sum partial_i phi0*corrector_i, but the final displayed triangle inequality uses only w and phi0. The omitted corrector must be bounded separately to infer either(1.12) or the deterministic T used to close the base case.

The local regularity bound requires R comparable to the local random scale, whereas Theorem1.3 covers every specified vertex. The proof does not provide the complementary near-boundary argument or simultaneous spatial control.
additional_scope_notes: The wavelength rescaling printed on PDF14 is inconsistent with the rescaled eigenvalue; the correct wavelength is L/sqrt(lambda0).

Interior estimates alone do not provide a global Hessian supremum on all allowed convex domains. A sector with opening omega in(pi/2,pi) has a Dirichlet eigenfunction with Hessian singularity r^(pi/omega-2). A boundary cutoff or integrable derivative formulation is needed.
The core helper separately handles the residual sign/projection and eigenvalue multiplicity/gap problems; they should not be double-counted as additional findings here.
counterevidence_and_limits: At a fixed center, retaining the random multiplier gives a meaningful stochastic estimate with an appropriate tail exponent, conditional on the imported regularity assumptions and boundary scale.
A corrected result may follow from stronger uniform stochastic estimates, a controlled corrector term and a valid spectral projection argument. No claim is made that such a result is impossible.
The cited external corrector and regularity theorems were not newly read or verified by this helper.
findings.impact: The printed argument does not establish the claimed deterministic all-vertex/all-edge convergence rate, and the resulting supremum bound is also used to choose T in the spectral proof.
findings.recommended_action: Retain or rigorously control the spatial random factors, state the local interior event, include the corrector contribution, and use the correctly scaled regularity estimate before asserting the deterministic conclusion.

editorial_notes.note: The denominator in(1.13) should use distance to the boundary, not distance to U0 itself.
The negative-norm duality numerator is printed as H1 on PDF8, while its later use is L2 duality.
Retain ellipticity/alpha dependence in Lemma A.1's constant; reconcile the extra L^-2 factor in(A.5) with(2.16).

actual_checks.role: Primary executor reviewer-authored analytic and symbolic checks, not independent acceptance

exact_symbolic_result.general_trace_argument: Off-diagonal entries do not affect the trace contraction with the scalar Hessian; no specific homogenized matrix is assumed.

checks.location: Theorem1.1 and equations1.3-1.4, PDF2-3; invocation2.15, PDF12
checks.claim: The written point-sampled relative-L2 homogenization estimate cannot hold uniformly for all smooth Dirichlet functions.
checks.proof: Fix any finite admissible graph realization with an interior vertex x0 and invertible Dirichlet matrix A_g=-L. Choose rho below the distance to every other sampled point and to the boundary. Let chi be a smooth compactly supported cutoff equal to1 near0 and set ubar_rho(x)=-|x-x0|^2 chi((x-x0)/rho)/(2 tr(abar)). Then ubar_rho is smooth and compactly supported in U_m; all sampled values are0. Its pointwise forcing -div(abar grad ubar_rho) is1 at x0 and0 at all other sampled points. Hence the discrete solution is A_g^(-1)e_x0, a fixed nonzero vector independent ofrho. The left side of1.4 is its positive discrete norm. The continuum L2 norm is O(rho^(2+d/2)) (with fixed domain-normalization factor), so the claimed right side tends to0. This contradicts every finite constant C for that realization.
checks.quantifiers: The source states one event and one C(d,alpha,U0) for every ubar in H2 intersect H01. A graph-dependent smooth witness is therefore legitimate for testing the asserted uniform event. No numerical Poisson simulation is needed; the argument applies to every nontrivial realization satisfying the asserted uniqueness.
checks.counterevidence: The argument uses smooth functions, so it does not rely merely on the ill-defined point evaluation of an H2 equivalence class. The intended interior equation and boundary-shell zero condition are used despite obvious reversed/missing-boundary symbols in the text. No averaging or bandwidth restriction is stated in1.3.
checks.scope: Refutes the displayed restatement and its unrestricted application in this acquired v1. It does not claim the external AV23b theorem or the final journal article was read or refuted.
checks.repair: Specify a legitimate sampling/coarse-graining map and the actual regularity or frequency-dependent homogenization estimate; recheck the variational applications. Replacing only the norm label is not a verified full repair.

checks.claim: Fixed-function concentration cannot justify the maximum over the stated continuous variational classes; uniform empirical normalization on those classes is false.
checks.proof: The competitors in2.8/2.20 are continuous L2 functions, not required to have zero boundary trace. Take an allowed d>=3 domain for which the displayed sup cap has strict slack above1 (a sufficiently small U0 makes lambda_0,1 large; alternatively A_T has this slack for sufficiently large T). For any finite realized set of sampled points, choose disjoint smooth cutoffs equal to0 at the points and1 outside tiny balls of radiusrho. Their product h_rho converges to1 in normalized L2, is bounded by1, and has averaged gradient energy O(N rho^(d-2)), tending to0. Let f_rho=h_rho/||h_rho||_L2. Then continuum normalized L2 equals1, sup norm tends to1, and gradient energy tends to0, hence both bounds in2.8 hold for smallrho. Yet every sampled value is0. Replacing the zero cutoff values byeta>0 gives positive denominators arbitrarily close to0 with the same bounds. Thus uniform empirical normalization fails even with smooth competitors, independently of ellipticity constants.
checks.scope: The declared class genuinely contains all these continuous trial functions; the proof does not restrict its maxima to a fixed finite-dimensional spectral space. This is a pathwise obstruction to the uniform step, not a disproof of every possible fixed-function concentration statement.
checks.counterevidence: The proof expressly permits these non-Dirichlet forcing/trial functions. A comparison using a single deterministic ground state may avoid one maximum, but does not repair the opposite random maximum. No assertion is made that the original ground state's unweighted energy equals the eigenvalue for a general homogenized matrix.
checks.repair: Use controlled finite-dimensional trial spaces or valid interpolation maps and prove the required simultaneous graph-dependent concentration. Track T and spectral-index event probabilities. No complete repaired proof is certified.

checks.claim: The printed H^-1 duality formula uses the H1 inner product and therefore defines the H1 norm on the Dirichlet subspace.
checks.proof: For nonzero Dirichlet f, Cauchy-Schwarz bounds sup_g <f,g>_H1/||g||_H1 by||f||_H1, and choosingg=f attains equality. The usual negative norm uses the L2/function-dual pairing againstg, divided by||g||_H1.
checks.repair: Replace the numerator by the intended distribution/L2 pairing and make its normalization consistent. Imported H^-1 bounds should be read only with that corrected definition.

checks.location: Graph energy, reciprocal spectral scaling and stochastic notation, PDF8-10,13
checks.proof: For the intended symmetric nonnegative unit-radius kernel and zero boundary shell, the graph energy identity makes -L positive definite on the interior Dirichlet space when every relevant component meets the boundary. Its inverse has positive eigenvalues and the ordinary finite-dimensional minmax principle applies. The continuum constant-SPD Dirichlet inverse is compact and self-adjoint, with mu_0,k=R^2/lambda_0,k. If |mu_m-mu_0|<=C L_m sqrt(mu_0) and the relative error is <=1/2, inversion gives |R^2 lambda_m-lambda_0|<=2C L_m lambda_0^(3/2)/R. Thus the desired exponent follows conditionally from a valid inverse-eigenvalue estimate. Markov's inequality applied to E exp((X/theta)^s)<=2 gives the stated stretched-exponential tail.
checks.limits: This algebra does not supply the missing comparison between continuous and sampled Hilbert spaces, nor a uniform stochastic event. No source optimality lower bound or external homogenization theorem is independently certified.

revision.reason: Refine R2 to constant-based trial functions, eliminating unnecessary ground-state/ellipticity qualification. Original receipt retained unchanged. All other exact and analytic checks and actual view records reused from hash-identical predecessor; not relabeled as newly executed.
